name: Lazarus Pharmaceuticals Hematic Sentinel Array — 'The Warden'
product_name: Lazarus Pharmaceuticals Hematic Sentinel Array — 'The Warden'
description: The Warden is an advanced internal biomonitor implant system consisting of a primary processing node embedded near the sternum and a distributed network of nanoscale sensor filaments threaded through the cardiovascular system, monitoring blood chemistry in real time. The system continuously analyzes for over 340 compounds — including toxins, pathogens, sedatives, neurotoxins, coagulants, performance-affecting substances, and a library of known assassination compounds — and alerts the host through a haptic pulse to the sternum when a threshold is crossed. More critically, the Warden carries an integrated response module: a pressurized microdosing reservoir containing Lazarus-formulated countermeasure compounds that can be automatically or manually deployed into the bloodstream within seconds of detection.

cultural_context: In Meridian 88's upper tiers, the Warden has become a quiet necessity for anyone with enemies sophisticated enough to use chemistry. Corporate executives, senior fixers, and political figures who operate in environments where a poisoned drink is a plausible threat consider it basic due diligence. Lazarus markets it with the tagline 'Know What's In You,' which has taken on uncomfortable resonance in a city where what's in your blood is increasingly not your own business. There is a grey market for the reservoir cartridges loaded with non-approved compounds — Lazarus's proprietary applicator is the bottleneck, and cracking it is a cottage industry.
known_users: Senior fixers operating in high-stakes political environments
Lazarus Pharmaceuticals' own executive protection staff
Assassination-aware underworld figures with long enemy lists
Undercover operatives who cannot control what they consume in the field
story_hooks: A client's Warden fired an automated countermeasure response — but the compound it flagged isn't in the standard library, meaning someone dosed them with something Lazarus hasn't catalogued yet. Finding the source means finding whoever is ahead of Lazarus's chemists.

The crew is hired to get close to a target known to carry a Warden — which means any chemical approach is off the table. Or is it? Someone is selling a compound that sits just below the Warden's detection threshold.

A Lazarus firmware update pushed to all Warden units in the city has quietly added a new compound to the monitoring list — one that's only present in people who've taken a specific Lazarus pharmaceutical. Users are being flagged and their location data is going somewhere.

A player character's Warden fires in the middle of a routine dinner — but every test they can run shows nothing in their blood. Either the implant is malfunctioning, or whatever was dosed into them has already been neutralized, and someone is watching to see what they do next.
